features.title: agent-comms
features.tldr: The handoff-v1 JSON contract agents emit, its stdlib validator behind `dadaia reports`, and ack-on-consume deletion.
features.summary: Agent-to-agent coordination is a JSON handoff under the workspace handoff tree, validated against the packaged handoff-v1 schema, with HTML reports as optional evidence.

features.title: agent-orchestration
features.tldr: Nine core Layer-1 roles, two dispatchers, document-governed ordered work, and advisory-only concurrency.
features.summary: Role ownership, dispatch purity, task discipline and review checkpoints; the ordered lifecycle is carried by SDD documents and agent dispatch, never by a runtime.

features.title: agentic-entities
features.tldr: Abstract-entity registry — Personas, Behaviors, Rules — plus the behavior map binding every skill and scoped rule file to one law section.
features.summary: The entity registry defines the workspace method abstractly and every scaffolded sub-agent, hook and rule file derives from it; the behavior map binds each skill and scoped rule file to one law section.

features.title: brand-identity
features.tldr: The brand — the dadaia-workspace slug, the rhino mark and the five-colour palette — for the docs site and launch assets; no in-package UI carries it any more.
features.summary: The canonical palette and mark survive the panel's demolition as the brand for public presence (docs site, README, launch assets); they live in the repository's public assets, never in a served UI.

features.title: public-asset-distribution
features.tldr: Public assets staged once, projected into the authored set (root map, scoped AGENTS.md, .agents/skills, .agents/agents); .claude/ entries are symlinks.
features.summary: The stage, install and doctor chain distributing the agentic surface into runtime roots, with hash-compare overwrite, rendered agents, whole-folder skills and a privacy gate.

features.title: pypi-distribution
features.tldr: The published PyPI package on one version axis, the OIDC publish pipeline, and the wheel content contract.
features.summary: dadaia-workspace publishes to PyPI from the release workflow under OIDC trusted publishing; pyproject version is the single source of the number, and minting is separate from publishing.

features.title: harness-claude-code
features.tldr: Entry harness with native sub-agent dispatch; reads the root AGENTS.md map natively and reaches skills and personas through per-entry symlinks into .agents/.
features.summary: How Claude Code loads the workspace law, attaches scoped law, dispatches the three dd- personas, and which hooks and gates it runs; the CLAUDE.md bridge and the DADAIA.md chain died at 0.4.7 candidate 6 (ADR 0017).

features.title: harness-codex
features.tldr: Entry harness on the Codex CLI — native AGENTS.md chain and .agents/skills; .codex/ carries config, hooks, Starlark rules and the persona TOML transcode.
features.summary: Codex reads the root map, the root->cwd AGENTS.md chain and .agents/skills natively; .codex/ holds config.toml, hooks.json, rules and the three dd- persona TOMLs transcoded from .agents/agents/. The .codex/skills copies and the DADAIA.md mirror died at 0.4.7 candidate 6.

features.title: harness-kimi-code
features.tldr: Layer-1 harness with an empty projection set — reads root AGENTS.md, .agents/skills and .agents/agents natively; user-level hook shims; DADAIA_CONTEXT binding.
features.summary: Kimi Code consumes the universal authored set directly; the .kimi-code/ mirror died at 0.4.7 candidate 6 (ADR 0017). Hooks stay user-level shims; binding is the exported DADAIA_CONTEXT.

features.title: product-vision
features.tldr: One workspace folder, an agent at its root, projects in repos inside, governance outside every repo; multi-project x multi-repo, never a monorepo; no slop.
features.summary: The founding paradigm and the pillars of dadaia-workspace, plus the two usage paths (a human from a shell, an agent from the root AGENTS.md map).

features.title: spec-context-project
features.tldr: One canonical specs tree owned by one main repository, optionally spanning associated repos, bound per session and safe for visible concurrent work.
features.summary: The central unit of dadaia-workspace — one main repository is the sole source of specs, bind, memory, releases and backlog, and associated repositories extend it without a second specs tree.

features.title: Consumer validation gate
features.tldr: A consumer-side validation agent running the shipped recipe on a real workspace is the release gate; no wheel publishes until every statement reports PASS.
features.summary: The canonical release gate is a consumer-side validation agent running the shipped recipe on a real workspace; a deterministic internal gate never approves a release by itself.

features.title: context-management
features.tldr: ALIVE/DEAD registry of one main repo plus N associated repos, one Invocation per process, a Bind carrying scope, bind-driven injection.
features.summary: Contexts (Spec Context Projects) and their repositories through a v3 registry, one resolution authority whose Bind carries the session's scope, one repo accessor, bind-driven injection.

features.title: cross-platform-portability
features.tldr: Linux, macOS and Windows through one platform capability seam, injected adapters, Python hooks and hard-gated cross-OS CI legs.
features.summary: core/platform.py is the single capability seam and the container selects adapters; security failures are loud, non-security features degrade explicitly, unsupported capabilities fail at construction.

features.title: server-registry
features.tldr: Port registry with TTL and PID tracking so parallel agents' dev servers never collide, owned by one stdlib script under the dd-cli-library skill.
features.summary: A JSON registry of dev-server ports with TTL and PID tracking, an expiry sweeper and a read-only scan against real OS listeners — read and written only by `dd-cli-library/scripts/registry.py`; no CLI verb.

features.title: workspace-doctor
features.tldr: The one compliance surface — dadaia doctor scores workspace, specs and ledgers from one rule record; --fix is the reaper, moving slop, deleting only by TTL.
features.summary: dadaia doctor runs the workspace walk, the specs rules and the ledger schema rules from one rule record, prints one line per finding and one compliance score per section plus a total, exits 1 on any error-class finding with a runnable fix line, and its reaper moves slop into a held zone and deletes only what a TTL expired.

features.title: workspace-init
features.tldr: Idempotent bootstrap of workspace state, the Python venv, the selected harness projections and the governance hooks.
features.summary: dadaia init provisions the venv, creates the registry's init zones and the selected harness roots, seeds the state files and the harness profile, then stages and installs public assets.

features.title: audits-canon
features.tldr: Audits are committed spec artifacts — three pillars over a sha window, JSONL findings moved by dadaia audit disposition, archived by dadaia audit close.
features.summary: An audit is a committed folder holding AUDIT.md and FINDINGS.jsonl; three pillars always run together over the window since the newest archived audit; a finding's disposition and the archive are two CLI verbs, each all-or-nothing and each leaving one governance event.

features.title: sdd-bug-backlog-governance
features.tldr: One bug record shape with no derived cache, one verb per governance record change, and every committed record schema-validated by dadaia doctor.
features.summary: The bug record store, the backlog live photo, the release state document and the decision record store — one record per bug with no git-derived cache, one histo-record-v1 shape for every exit, every record change a CLI verb, every committed record schema-validated by dadaia doctor.

features.title: sdd-gate-v3
features.tldr: No-lock enforcement — three gate blocks (root entry, non-venv command, PROTECTED or out-of-scope write), one fix line per BLOCK, chokepoints at the push.
features.summary: The merged PreToolUse gate blocks exactly three things and reads no SDD artifact; every refusal anywhere carries one executable fix line; the git chokepoints enforce the publication boundary and the full denylist scan over every pushed path.
